before.title: Demand pattern
before.body: Sheraton demand follows market seasonality plus Bonvoy campaign calendars. Treat portfolio averages as directional only until property pace data exists.

before.title: Competitive pressure
before.body: Same-market Marriott sister brands can both help (Bonvoy shoppers) and cannibalize. Map sister-brand density before assuming exclusive Bonvoy capture for Sheraton.

before.title: Conversion workstream
before.body: Systems, content, and rate integrity at cutover determine whether platform demand actually books the hotel in week one.

before.title: What is differentiated commercially
before.body: Upper-upscale full-service Marriott brand oriented to gatherings, club spaces, and destination public areas inside Marriott Bonvoy. Commercially, the brand case is Bonvoy + Marriott channels applied to a distinct Sheraton product — not a generic Marriott International story.

after.title: What is differentiated commercially
after.body: Upper-upscale full-service Marriott brand oriented to gatherings, club spaces, and destination public areas inside Marriott Bonvoy. Commercially, the brand case is Bonvoy + Marriott channels applied to a distinct Sheraton product — not a generic Marriott International story.

before.title: Commercial engine
before.body: Sheraton sells through Marriott International distribution and Marriott Bonvoy while the brand product must still win the stay. Commercial diligence should separate platform reach from Sheraton conversion on the property.

after.title: Commercial Engine
after.body: Sheraton commercial distribution rides Marriott Bonvoy direct channels, GDS, OTAs, and parent sales systems. Full-service upscale social & meetings: lobby energy, gatherings, and Bonvoy for travelers who want Sheraton community cues with Marriott commercial systems. Owners should underwrite channel mix and loyalty contribution for this asset—not corporate averages alone.
